items.name: Quickmini
items.blurb: Drop in a video, choose how hard to compress it, optionally cut sections out, export. The whole encode runs in your tab through ffmpeg.wasm — the file never leaves your machine. Trimming and compressing happen in a single ffmpeg pass, and cut footage is never decoded, which took an 11 MB export from 25s down to 5.8s.

items.name: Cutaway
items.blurb: The first pass at the same problem: mark in and out points on a timeline, keep several sections, export the joined result. Quickmini grew out of it once it became clear that compressing an untouched video was the common case, not trimming.

items.name: DivideNConquer
items.blurb: Turns a prompt — an equation, a theorem, a “how does X work” — into an interactive hierarchical knowledge graph you can expand, rearrange and export. KaTeX renders the mathematics fully offline with MathML for screen readers, so it works with no network at all.

items.name: loop-runner
items.blurb: An agent-agnostic, human-in-the-loop engineering runner. Point it at a git repository: it drafts a plan, you approve it, it implements the change with whichever agent you choose, opens a pull request — and stops. Nothing merges without you.

items.name: Traddy
items.blurb: A portfolio and trading interface for Interactive Brokers. FastAPI and ib_async talk to IB Gateway; the front end is Vite, React, TypeScript and Tailwind.

items.name: AIWC website
items.blurb: Rebuilt the Australia India Water Centre's site as a single self-contained HTML file — no framework, no build step, no CDN — served straight from a GitHub Pages branch. Eight sections, a client-side search over every profile, and a full local copy of the original media.
